feedback.problem:
Given that for $s>0,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of $f(t)=-3\operatorname{cos}⁡5t+6\operatorname{sin}⁡5t$ for $s>0.$

$L{f(t)}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{-3\operatorname{cos}⁡5t+6\operatorname{sin}⁡5t} & =L{-3\operatorname{cos}⁡5t}+L{6\operatorname{sin}⁡5t} \\  & =-3L{\operatorname{cos}⁡5t}+6L{\operatorname{sin}⁡5t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t} & =\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0, \\ L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡5t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+25},\,s>0 \\ L{\operatorname{sin}⁡5t} & =\frac{5}{{s}^{2}+25},\,s>0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =-3L{\operatorname{cos}⁡5t}+6L{\operatorname{sin}⁡5t} \\  & =-3\cdot \frac{s}{{s}^{2}+25}+6\cdot \frac{5}{{s}^{2}+25} \\  & =-\frac{3s}{{s}^{2}+25}+\frac{30}{{s}^{2}+25} \\  & =\frac{-3s+30}{{s}^{2}+25}.\end{aligned}
$$
